findings.statement: TNFa and NFkB are the most uniformly and strongly activated PROGENy pathways in inflamed UC mucosa (up in five of five cohorts); TNFa reaches its highest t in GSE206285 [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=20.07]. This fits the established anti-TNF target but is a broad inflammatory readout.

JAK-STAT pathway activity is up in five of five cohorts, for example in GSE193677 [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=15.68]. This is consistent with the approved JAK inhibitor class.

STAT3 regulon activity is up in five of five cohorts, for example in GSE206285 [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=24.0]. It is the central JAK-STAT effector; activity is inferred from target genes, not from STAT3 mRNA.

EGFR, MAPK, PI3K, TGFb, hypoxia, VEGF and estrogen pathways are also up in five of five cohorts, and the top TF list is dominated by stress and AP1/ATF family members (AP1 in GSE193677 [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=18.4]). These are non-specific: inflamed mucosa activates many programs at once, so they are weak for target prioritisation compared with specific circuits.

p53 pathway activity is down in three of five cohorts and not up in any (GSE16879 [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE16879.t=-3.59]), so it is not a consistent signature. WNT and Trail are up in four of five cohorts, not all five.

CXCR2 is rank 1 in the convergence ranking: up in five of five cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.264]), with strong genetics and literature support, and with clinical-stage antagonists (reparixin Phase 3, navarixin, ladarixin and SX-682 Phase 2), none approved for UC.

In the single-cell data the CXCR2 transcript is almost entirely neutrophil-derived (neutrophil share of transcripts in inflamed mucosa [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]). Without neutrophils, as in Smillie, it maps to T/NK cells at a very low fraction of cells expressing and does not replicate. The bulk increase therefore largely reflects neutrophil infiltration, not a change of the epithelium or stroma, so CXCR2 acts as a neutrophil-recruitment target.

CXCL8 transcripts in inflamed mucosa come mainly from neutrophil states (neutrophil share of transcripts [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]), led by Neutrophil CXCR4, Neutrophil and Neutrophil OSM. In Smillie, which has no neutrophils, macrophages dominate, so the cell source depends on dataset capture. CXCL8 has only phase 2 anti-IL-8 antibodies (ABX-IL8, adakitug).

Circuit CXCL8 (Neutrophil CXCR4) to CXCR2 (Neutrophil) is a neutrophil-to-neutrophil loop whose co-expression score rises in inflamed UC mucosa (log2 change vs uninflamed [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=2.755]). Co-expression is not proof of signalling.

Neutrophil CXCL8 is also co-expressed with ACKR1 on ACKR1 endothelial cells (log2 change vs uninflamed for the generic Neutrophil sender [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=1.991]), a candidate neutrophil-to-venule recruitment axis. ACKR1 is an atypical chemokine receptor and no ACKR1-directed drug was found. Co-expression only.

IL1B from monocyte-derived macrophages is co-expressed with IL1R2 on neutrophil states (log2 change vs uninflamed for Neutrophil CXCR4 as receiver [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=2.059]). IL1R2 is a decoy receptor, so this score does not imply signalling. IL1B is drug-tractable (canakinumab approved in other indications) but has no UC approval.

Negative result: the neutrophil-OSM to IL6ST on LP fibroblast circuit has a low score in inflamed mucosa and falls versus uninflamed (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=-0.709]). The Gubatan data do not support a strong neutrophil OSM to inflammatory fibroblast signal. The only increase is Neutrophil PADI4 to LP fibroblast, from a zero baseline score.

CHI3L1 is among the strongest replicated up-regulated genes (meta log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.7135], five of five cohorts) and has no drug, as is also true of AQP9, DUOX2 and CXCL1 in the top-ranked list. It is better framed as a biomarker or undrugged candidate than a validated target.

caveats: PROGENy and CollecTRI activities are inferred from bulk biopsies; shifts in cell composition (neutrophil and macrophage infiltration) can drive them and cannot be separated from within-cell signalling.
Ligand-receptor scores are co-expression of mean CP10K, not evidence of signalling; IL1R2 is a decoy receptor and ACKR1 is atypical.
Bulk cohort comparisons are inflamed or UC versus control, whereas communication scores compare inflamed with uninflamed UC mucosa in one single-cell dataset (Gubatan 2026).
Neutrophils are absent from Smillie 2019, so cell-source calls for neutrophil genes (CXCL8, CXCR2) depend on the dataset used.
IL-23 and integrin pathways were not directly assessed because PROGENy has no such pathway; JAK-STAT and TNFa activity are the proxies for approved drug classes.
Pathways active in five cohorts include many non-specific programs; specific circuits are preferred.
